q-32517.name: Question 1
q-32517.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=-4 \\  & {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
q-32517.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now   

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}=4 \\  & {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ Since we have that ${x}_{1}=4$,  we only need to find ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=4 \\ {x}_{2}=-6-2{x}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Consider the system of linear equations {2x1+2x2+4x3=−4x2+2x3=−6. Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
[−4x26−2x2],x2∈(−∞,∞)
b
[4x26+x2],x2∈(−∞,∞)
c
[8−6+x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
d
[4−6−2x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
e
[6−4−2x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[224−4012−6].

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

M=[224−4012−6]R1:=12R1∼[112−2012−6]R1:=R1+(−1)R2∼[1004012−6]

The corresponding system is now

{x1=4x2+2x3=−6. The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x1 and x2, and we have one free variable, x3. Since we have that x1=4, we only need to find x2 in terms of x3.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x1=4x2=−6−2x3,

where x3 (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

[x1x2x3]=[4−6−2x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞).

q-74638.name: Question 2
q-74638.problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 3x+2y=-3 \\  & -6x-4y=6,\end{aligned}
$$

which of the following statements are true?

I. The system is consistent independent

II. The system is consistent dependent

III. The system has no solution
q-74638.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find the solution to the system. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -3 \\ -6 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -3 \\ -6 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 3x+2y=-3 \\  & 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
3x+2y=-3
$$

The basic variable is $x,$ and we have a free variable $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*.

As a result, only statement II is true.

q-74691.name: Question 3
q-74691.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 2x-2y=4 \\  & -3x+ky=-6\end{aligned}
$$
q-74691.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & k & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & k & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & k-3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 2x-2y=4 \\  & (k-3)y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=3,$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$,. So, we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $2x+2y=4.$ 

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=3.$

q-131721.name: Question 4
q-131721.problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x+2y=-1 \\  & 3x+7y=1 \\  & -2x-4y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. The system is consistent independent

II. The system has no solution

III. The system is consistent dependent
q-131721.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 \\ -2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 \\ -2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y=-1 \\ y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation we have $y=4$ and substituting this into the first equation yields $x=-9.$ So,  we conclude that the system is consistent independent. 

As a result, only statement I is true.

q-131723.name: Question 5
q-131723.problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-y+z=3 \\  & -3x+3y-3z=10\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. The system is inconsistent

II. The system has a unique solution

III. The system is consistent dependent
q-131723.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & -3 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & -3 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 19\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y+0z=19,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement I is true.
